newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London steady in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London steady in thin trade.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were steady on Monday, supported by Tokyo's higher close but trading was minimal with investors still reluctant to commit funds in the face of nagging political worries.
In London, the Nikkei/Ise 50 index was up 4.83 points at 1,420.16 in thin afternoon dealing.
"Tokyo moved higher on incredibly thin volume and that has followed through into London," one dealer said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 ended 0.70 percent higher in what dealers called lacklustre trade as wary investors sat back to survey the still uncertain political landscape.
Traders said the inactivity in both markets -- Tokyo closed with volume at a meagre 198 million shares -- was surprising in light of the dollar's strength.
"The dollar's move above 114 yen should really have spurred activity in stocks with a high export ratio. When you get a move like this, you would expect a major reaction," the dealer said.
Dealers said shares were broadly steady, although Honda had appeared to squeeze more benefit than most from the strong dollar.
